topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture on complement, framing its biological importance and complex nomenclature.

topics.label: Foundations and central C3 activation in complement
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the foundational principles, nomenclature rules, and the central role of C3 cleavage in complement activation.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the three distinct upstream pathways and mechanisms that drive complement activation to reach the trigger threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the primary downstream effector mechanisms by which complement clears pathogens and drives inflammation.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: It details the regulatory factors and mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the distinct clinical manifestations and disease susceptibilities resulting from deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the evolutionary strategies and molecular mechanisms used by pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus to evade complement destruction.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
